content.text:
networks:
  wims_internal:
    driver: bridge
    name: wims_internal
    # Pen-test follow-up 2026-06-29: explicit subnet + static IPs for redis,
    # postgres, keycloak, openbao, and ollama. These IPs are referenced by
    # extra_hosts entries that bypass broken Docker DNS after wims_internal
    # network recreation on the live VPS (see PR #485-#487).
    # Keep dynamic allocations in 172.18.0.128/25 so short-lived/dynamic
    # containers cannot claim the low static addresses during parallel Compose
    # startup (observed as Docker 28 "Address already in use" in CI).
    ipam:
      config:
        - subnet: 172.18.0.0/24
          ip_range: 172.18.0.128/25

services:
  # --- Infrastructure & Databases ---
  postgres:
    image: postgis/postgis:15-3.4-alpine
    container_name: wims-postgres
    command: ["postgres", "-c", "shared_buffers=2GB", "-c", "max_connections=75"]
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: postgres
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?error}
      POSTGRES_DB: wims
    volumes:
      - postgres_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
      - ./postgres-init:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d:ro
    networks:
      wims_internal:
        ipv4_address: 172.18.0.3
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U postgres -d wims"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
    restart: always
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:5432:5432"

  redis:
    image: redis:7.2-alpine
    container_name: wims-redis
    command: ["redis-server", "--maxmemory", "512mb", "--maxmemory-policy", "allkeys-lru"]
    # Pen-test follow-up 2026-06-29: pin redis to 172.18.0.5 (the IP the live
    # VPS was already using dynamically) so the wims-suricata `extra_hosts`
    # mapping below stays valid across `docker compose down && up` cycles.
    networks:
      wims_internal:
        ipv4_address: 172.18.0.5
    restart: always
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:6379:6379"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "ping"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 5

  mailhog:
    image: mailhog/mailhog:v1.0.1
    container_name: wims-mailhog
    networks:
      - wims_internal
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:1025:1025"
      - "127.0.0.1:8025:8025"

  keycloak:
    build: ./keycloak
    image: wims-keycloak-demo-otp:local
    container_name: wims-keycloak
    command: start-dev --import-realm
    # Pen-test follow-up 2026-06-29 (deploy fix): the `ipam.config.subnet`
    # added in PR #485 causes the wims_internal network to be recreated on
    # deploy. After recreation, the Docker embedded DNS does NOT consistently
    # resolve `postgres` from this keycloak container (verified on the live
    # VPS — `getent hosts postgres` returns empty even after a fresh
    # container recreate, while TCP to the static IP works). Inject the
    # mapping directly into /etc/hosts to bypass the broken DNS. Same fix
    # pattern as the wims-suricata `extra_hosts` in PR #485.
    extra_hosts:
      - "postgres:172.18.0.3"
      - "redis:172.18.0.5"
    volumes:
      - ./keycloak/import:/opt/keycloak/data/import:ro
      - ./keycloak/themes/wims-bfp:/opt/keycloak/themes/wims-bfp:ro
    environment:
      KC_DB: postgres
      KC_DB_URL: jdbc:postgresql://postgres:5432/keycloak
      KC_DB_USERNAME: keycloak
      KC_DB_PASSWORD: ${KC_DB_PASSWORD:?error}
      KEYCLOAK_ADMIN: ${KEYCLOAK_ADMIN:-admin}
      KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD: ${KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD:?error}
      KC_HTTP_RELATIVE_PATH: /auth
      KC_PROXY: edge
      KC_PROXY_HEADERS: xforwarded
      KC_HOSTNAME_STRICT: "false"
      KC_HOSTNAME_STRICT_BACKCHANNEL: "false"
      KC_HOSTNAME_URL: http://localhost:8080/auth
      KC_HTTP_ENABLED: "true"
      KC_LOG_LEVEL: INFO
      QUARKUS_TRANSACTION_MANAGER_ENABLE_RECOVERY: "true"
      # SMTP configuration (for Keycloak realm ${env.SMTP_*} placeholders)
      SMTP_HOST: ${SMTP_HOST:-smtp-relay.brevo.com}
      SMTP_PORT: ${SMTP_PORT:-2525}
      SMTP_FROM: ${SMTP_FROM:-noreply@wims-bfp.local}
      SMTP_FROM_DISPLAY: ${SMTP_FROM_DISPLAY:-WIMS-BFP}
      SMTP_REPLYTO: ${SMTP_REPLYTO:-no-reply@wimsbfp.tech}
      SMTP_REPLYTO_DISPLAY: ${SMTP_REPLYTO_DISPLAY:-WIMS-BFP No Reply}
      SMTP_SSL: ${SMTP_SSL:-false}
      SMTP_STARTTLS: ${SMTP_STARTTLS:-true}
      SMTP_AUTH: ${SMTP_AUTH:-true}
      SMTP_USER: ${SMTP_USER:-}
      SMTP_PASSWORD: ${SMTP_PASSWORD:-}
      # WS-B (RP-08/RP-18): Keycloak → WIMS audit event push
      WIMS_AUDIT_INGEST_URL: http://backend:8000/api/auth/keycloak-event
      WIMS_KEYCLOAK_EVENT_SECRET: ${WIMS_KEYCLOAK_EVENT_SECRET:-}
    networks:
      wims_internal:
        ipv4_address: 172.18.0.7
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL","exec 3<>/dev/tcp/localhost/8080 && echo -e 'GET /auth/ HTTP/1.0\\r\\nHost: localhost\\r\\n\\r\\n' >&3 && timeout 8 cat <&3 | head -1 | grep -qE '^HTTP'"]
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 20
      start_period: 120s
    restart: always
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:8080:8080"

  keycloak-bootstrap:
    image: quay.io/keycloak/keycloak:24.0.0
    container_name: wims-keycloak-bootstrap
    entrypoint: ["/bin/sh", "/opt/keycloak/bootstrap/bootstrap-master-realm.sh"]
    volumes:
      - ./keycloak/bootstrap:/opt/keycloak/bootstrap:ro
    environment:
      KEYCLOAK_URL: http://keycloak:8080/auth
      KEYCLOAK_ADMIN: ${KEYCLOAK_ADMIN:-admin}
      KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD: ${KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD:?error}
    networks:
      - wims_internal
    depends_on:
      keycloak:
        condition: service_healthy
    restart: "no"

  # --- Key Management (OpenBao) ---
  openbao:
    image: openbao/openbao:2.2.0
    container_name: wims-openbao
    cap_add:
      - IPC_LOCK
    volumes:
      - openbao_data:/vault/file
      - ./openbao/config:/vault/config:ro
    environment:
      BAO_SKIP_VERIFY: "true"
    networks:
      wims_internal:
        ipv4_address: 172.18.0.8
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "bao status -address=http://localhost:8200 -format=json >/tmp/hc.json 2>/dev/null && grep -q initialized.*true /tmp/hc.json && grep -q sealed.*false /tmp/hc.json"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 10
      start_period: 10s
    restart: always
    entrypoint: ["bao", "server", "-config=/vault/config/openbao.hcl"]

  openbao-bootstrap:
    image: openbao/openbao:2.2.0
    container_name: wims-openbao-bootstrap
    entrypoint: ["/bin/sh", "/vault/init/bootstrap-openbao.sh"]
    volumes:
      - ./openbao/init:/vault/init:ro
      - ./openbao/config:/vault/config:ro
      - openbao_data:/vault/file
    environment:
      OPENBAO_ADDR: http://openbao:8200
      OPENBAO_TOKEN: ${OPENBAO_TOKEN:-}
      OPENBAO_UNSEAL_KEY: ${OPENBAO_UNSEAL_KEY:-}
      OPENBAO_DEV_ROOT_TOKEN: ${OPENBAO_DEV_ROOT_TOKEN:-devroot}
    extra_hosts:
      - "openbao:172.18.0.8"
    networks:
      - wims_internal
    depends_on:
      openbao:
        condition: service_started
    restart: "no"

  ollama:
    image: ollama/ollama:0.5.1
    container_name: wims-ollama
    volumes:
      - ollama_data:/root/.ollama
    networks:
      wims_internal:
        ipv4_address: 172.18.0.4
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "ollama", "list"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 30
      start_period: 30s
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: '4'
          memory: 6gb
    restart: always

  ollama-model-pull:
    image: ollama/ollama:0.5.1
    container_name: wims-ollama-model-pull
    command: pull qwen2.5:3b
    environment:
      - OLLAMA_HOST=http://ollama:11434
    extra_hosts:
      - "ollama:172.18.0.4"
    networks:
      - wims_internal
    depends_on:
      ollama:
        condition: service_healthy
    restart: "no"

  # --- Applications ---
  backend:
    build: ./backend
    container_name: wims-backend
    # Pen-test follow-up 2026-06-29 (deploy fix): see keycloak comment above
    # for rationale. Same Docker DNS unreliability after wims_internal
    # network recreation. Inject the 4 hostnames the backend connects to
    # (postgres, redis, keycloak, ollama) into /etc/hosts.
    extra_hosts:
      - "postgres:172.18.0.3"
      - "redis:172.18.0.5"
      - "keycloak:172.18.0.7"
      - "ollama:172.18.0.4"
    environment:
      - DATABASE_URL=postgresql://wims_app_user:wimsapp@postgres:5432/wims
      - DATABASE_ADMIN_URL=postgresql://postgres:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?error}@postgres:5432/wims
      - PYTHONPATH=/app
      - REDIS_URL=redis://redis:6379/0
      - KEYCLOAK_REALM_URL=http://keycloak:8080/auth/realms/bfp
      - KEYCLOAK_ISSUER=http://localhost:8080/auth/realms/bfp
      - KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_ID=wims-web
      - KEYCLOAK_AUDIENCE=wims-web
      - KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_CLIENT_ID=${KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_CLIENT_ID:-}
      - KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_CLIENT_SECRET=${KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_CLIENT_SECRET:-}
      - KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_USER=${KEYCLOAK_ADMIN:-admin}
      - KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD=${KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD:?error}
      - OLLAMA_URL=http://ollama:11434
      - SURICATA_EVE_PATH=/var/log/suricata/eve.json
      - AFOR_TEMPLATE_PATH=/app/AFOR-FORMATTED.xlsx
      - CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS=http://localhost,https://localhost,http://127.0.0.1,http://127.0.0.1:3000,http://localhost:8090,http://localhost:3000,http://localhost:8000
      - NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=http://localhost
      - OPENBAO_ADDR=${OPENBAO_ADDR:-http://openbao:8200}
      - OPENBAO_TOKEN=
      - OPENBAO_TOKEN_FILE=/openbao-creds/.wims-app-token
      - OPENBAO_TRANSIT_MOUNT=${OPENBAO_TRANSIT_MOUNT:-transit}
      - WIMS_CRYPTO_PROVIDER=${WIMS_CRYPTO_PROVIDER:-env_aesgcm}
      # WS-B (RP-08/RP-18): shared secret for Keycloak → WIMS audit event push
      - WIMS_KEYCLOAK_EVENT_SECRET=${WIMS_KEYCLOAK_EVENT_SECRET:-}
    volumes:
      - incident_attachments_data:/app/storage
      - ./suricata/logs:/var/log/suricata:ro
      - ./postgres-init:/postgres-init:ro
      - openbao_data:/openbao-creds:ro
    networks:
      - wims_internal
    env_file:
      - path: .env
        required: false
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy
      keycloak:
        condition: service_started
      keycloak-bootstrap:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
      ollama:
        condition: service_healthy
      ollama-model-pull:
        condition: service_completed_successfully

  celery-worker:
    build: ./backend
    container_name: wims-celery-worker
    command: celery -A main.celery_app worker --beat --loglevel=info
    # Pen-test follow-up 2026-06-29 (deploy fix): see keycloak comment above
    # for rationale. Same set of hostnames as the backend.
    extra_hosts:
      - "postgres:172.18.0.3"
      - "redis:172.18.0.5"
      - "keycloak:172.18.0.7"
      - "ollama:172.18.0.4"
    environment:
      - DATABASE_URL=postgresql://wims_app_user:wimsapp@postgres:5432/wims
      - REDIS_URL=redis://redis:6379/0
      - KEYCLOAK_REALM_URL=http://keycloak:8080/auth/realms/bfp
      - OLLAMA_URL=http://ollama:11434
      - SURICATA_EVE_PATH=/var/log/suricata/eve.json
      - EXPORT_DIR=/app/storage/exports
      - AFOR_TEMPLATE_PATH=/app/AFOR-FORMATTED.xlsx
      - NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=http://localhost
      - FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON=${FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON:-}
      - FIREBASE_CREDENTIALS_PATH=/app/firebase-creds.json
      - SMTP_HOST=${SMTP_HOST:-smtp-relay.brevo.com}
      - SMTP_PORT=${SMTP_PORT:-2525}
      - SMTP_FROM=${SMTP_FROM:-noreply@wims-bfp.local}
      - SMTP_USER=${SMTP_USER:-}
      - SMTP_PASSWORD=${SMTP_PASSWORD:-}
      - SMTP_STARTTLS=${SMTP_STARTTLS:-true}
      - OPENBAO_ADDR=${OPENBAO_ADDR:-http://openbao:8200}

# Trust the Docker bridge as the source of X-Forwarded-For. Nginx
    # resolves $remote_addr from the header instead of the socket IP so
    # per-IP rate-limit keys reflect the real client, not the container
    # bridge. The previous /12 (1,048,576 addrs) was 16x wider than
    # necessary and left X-Forwarded-For spoofing open on any other
    # endpoint that still reads $remote_addr (gap #14 followup, BLK-1).
    # Narrow the trusted-proxy range to the actual Docker Compose v2
    # default custom bridge subnet.
    set_real_ip_from  172.18.0.0/16;   # docker compose v2 default custom bridge
    set_real_ip_from  127.0.0.1;
    real_ip_header    X-Forwarded-For;
    real_ip_recursive on;

    # Per-IP rate-limit zones — stored in 10 MB shared memory.
    # public_api:   tight limit for the unauthenticated zero-trust DMZ endpoint.
    # civilian_api: mid-tier limit for the civilian report form (higher blast radius).

services:
  keycloak:
    environment:
      KC_HOSTNAME_URL: ${PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/auth

  backend:
    environment:
      - KEYCLOAK_ISSUER=${PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/auth/realms/bfp
      - CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS=${PUBLIC_BASE_URL}
      - NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=${PUBLIC_BASE_URL}
      - WIMS_MASTER_KEY=${WIMS_MASTER_KEY}

  celery-worker:
    environment:
      - NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=${PUBLIC_BASE_URL}
      - WIMS_MASTER_KEY=${WIMS_MASTER_KEY}

  frontend:
    build:
      args:
        NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL: /api
        NEXT_PUBLIC_AUTH_API_URL: /auth
        NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL: ${PUBLIC_BASE_URL}
        NEXT_PUBLIC_OIDC_REDIRECT_URI: ${PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/callback
        NEXT_PUBLIC_OIDC_AUTHORITY: ${PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/auth/realms/bfp
    environment:
      - NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=/api
      - NEXT_PUBLIC_AUTH_API_URL=/auth
      - NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL=${PUBLIC_BASE_URL}
      - NEXT_PUBLIC_OIDC_REDIRECT_URI=${PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/callback
      - NEXT_PUBLIC_OIDC_AUTHORITY=${PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/auth/realms/bfp
      - NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=${PUBLIC_BASE_URL}
      - AUTH_SERVER_URL=http://keycloak:8080/auth
      - BACKEND_URL=http://backend:8000

  # Contabo production VPS has 8 vCPUs / 23 GiB RAM.
  # Reserve half the CPU and 6 GB RAM for Qwen2.5-3B, leaving headroom for Postgres,
  # Keycloak, backend, Celery, Suricata, Redis, nginx, and the host OS cache.
  ollama:
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: '4'
          memory: 6gb

  # Production TLS certs — not available in local dev (override swaps nginx.conf).
  # nginx.conf mount is in the base compose file; this file only adds production certs.
  nginx-gateway:
    volumes:
      - ${LETSENCRYPT_DIR:-/opt/wims-bfp/letsencrypt}:/etc/letsencrypt:ro

45:**Host port exposure:** Only `nginx-gateway` intentionally binds public interfaces (`0.0.0.0:80` and `0.0.0.0:443`). Database and support/admin surfaces are bound to host loopback only: Postgres `127.0.0.1:5432`, Redis `127.0.0.1:6379`, MailHog `127.0.0.1:1025`/`8025`, and direct Keycloak `127.0.0.1:8080`. Browser and OIDC traffic should reach Keycloak only through nginx at `/auth/`.
69:## Nginx
71:**File:** `src/nginx/nginx.conf`
73:**Compose split:** `src/docker-compose.yml` is the dev-neutral base compose file. Production/VPS deployment uses the committed `src/docker-compose.prod.yml` override plus an uncommitted `src/.env.production` file. Local HTTP-only nginx testing uses `src/docker-compose.override.yml`, which mounts `src/nginx/nginx.local.conf` over the container config. The tracked `src/.env.production.example` documents required host values.
81:`src/nginx/nginx.local.conf` is local-development-only and intentionally omits TLS. It is loaded automatically by `src/docker-compose.override.yml` when running plain `docker compose ...` from `src/`. Do not deploy it to VPS/production.
89:**VPS nginx recovery command:**
92:docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml --env-file .env.production up -d --force-recreate nginx-gateway
95:Use explicit `-f` flags on the VPS. Plain `docker compose up` auto-loads `docker-compose.override.yml`, mounts `src/nginx/nginx.local.conf`, and publishes port 443 to an HTTP-only nginx process. The symptom is HTTP working while HTTPS fails with connection refused or an SSL EOF. The production command mounts `/etc/letsencrypt` into the container and loads `src/nginx/nginx.conf`, which terminates TLS for `wimsbfp.tech`.
99:**Operational note:** On 2026-05-26, a login outage occurred when the VPS services were running with only the base `docker-compose.yml` values. Public Keycloak discovery returned `403 {"error":"invalid_request","error_description":"HTTPS required"}` and/or advertised localhost/port-8080 auth URLs. Recreating Keycloak, backend, frontend, and nginx with the production override restored `KC_HOSTNAME_URL=${PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/auth`, backend `KEYCLOAK_ISSUER=${PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/auth/realms/bfp`, and frontend public auth build/runtime values. After the restart, `https://wimsbfp.tech/auth/realms/bfp/.well-known/openid-configuration` returned 200 and advertised `https://wimsbfp.tech/auth/...` endpoints only.
101:**GitOps deploy workflow:** `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` SSHs to the hardened VPS as the non-root `wims` user, using passwordless sudo only for root-owned certbot package/certificate/cron operations. It mirrors the production command above via a shell `compose()` helper that always includes `docker-compose.yml`, `docker-compose.prod.yml`, and `.env.production`. It validates `compose config --quiet`, checks DB connectivity, and rebuilds/restarts with `up -d --build --wait`. The `--wait` flag requires every service to be in "running" or "healthy" state. The `openbao-bootstrap` init container has no healthcheck and would normally exit after its script completes, causing `--wait` to fail. Its bootstrap script therefore ends with a keep-alive loop (`while true; do sleep 3600; done`) to stay in "running" state until the stack is torn down. Post-deploy checks cover backend-local `/health`, public nginx `/health`, Keycloak discovery, a real public backend route (`/api/public/emergency-services`), and the required Ollama model. The public backend probe catches stale nginx upstream addresses that nginx's self-served `/health` cannot detect. TLS provisioning skips issuance when `/etc/letsencrypt/live/wimsbfp.tech/` already contains a cert/key; first-time issuance uses certbot standalone and the renewal hook reloads the running nginx container with `docker exec wims-nginx-gateway nginx -s reload`.
105:**Current certificate state:** `src/nginx/nginx.conf` expects `/etc/letsencrypt/live/wimsbfp.tech/fullchain.pem` and `privkey.pem`. A Let’s Encrypt certificate for `wimsbfp.tech` was issued on the VPS on 2026-05-26 and certbot renewal is installed with an nginx reload hook.
107:**TLS mount:** `src/docker-compose.yml` no longer mounts certificate paths in the dev-neutral base service. Production TLS is added only by `src/docker-compose.prod.yml`, which binds `${LETSENCRYPT_DIR:-/opt/wims-bfp/letsencrypt}:/etc/letsencrypt:ro` for `wims-nginx-gateway`. On the VPS, `src/.env.production` sets `LETSENCRYPT_DIR=/etc/letsencrypt`, so the gateway receives the host certificate tree directly. Do not replace this with a repo-local symlink directory; Docker bind mounts expose the directory itself, so mounting `/opt/wims-bfp/letsencrypt` when it only contains `letsencrypt -> /etc/letsencrypt` hides the expected `/etc/letsencrypt/live/<domain>/...` paths from nginx.
109:**Docker DNS upstream refresh:** Both nginx configs use Docker's embedded resolver (`127.0.0.11`) and shared upstream zones with `server backend:8000 resolve` (`backend_servers`) and `server frontend:3000 resolve` (`frontend_servers`). Nginx refreshes both addresses after Compose recreates containers instead of retaining stale IPs and returning `502 Connection refused`. The deploy workflow also runs `nginx -s reload` after `compose up` as a safety net, and checks the frontend `/login` route post-deploy in addition to the existing Keycloak and API health probes.
113:**Ollama VPS resource cap:** The current Contabo production VPS has 8 vCPUs / 23 GiB RAM. `docker-compose.yml` and `docker-compose.prod.yml` cap Ollama at `cpus: '4'` / `memory: 6gb` for `qwen2.5:3b`. This reserves enough headroom for Qwen2.5-3B inference while leaving CPU and memory for Postgres, Keycloak, backend, Celery, Suricata, Redis, nginx, and the host OS cache. Older 2-vCPU / 8 GB VPS overrides must not be used on the Contabo host because they under-allocate the model and database services.
115:**Frontend/auth env:** `docker-compose.prod.yml` sets browser-facing frontend build/runtime variables to the public HTTPS origin (`${PUBLIC_BASE_URL}`) or relative paths (`/api`, `/auth`). The development compose file also uses relative `/api` and `/auth` for browser-facing access, so local HTTP desk checks stay same-origin and avoid CORS preflight redirects. The Next.js server-side auth routes use `BACKEND_URL=http://backend:8000` in both development and production, and route handlers append `/api/...` explicitly. `POST /api/auth/refresh` is also server-side and must use the internal Keycloak origin, so both development and production compose set `AUTH_SERVER_URL=http://keycloak:8080/auth`; do not substitute browser-relative `/auth` for this value. Keycloak advertises `KC_HOSTNAME_URL=${PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/auth` in production to keep OIDC discovery issuer/endpoints aligned with the nginx `/auth/` proxy path. For `POST /api/auth/sync`, the route forwards nginx-provided `X-Real-IP`/sanitized `X-Forwarded-For` to backend `POST /api/auth/callback` so backend Redis rate limiting keys by end-user IP rather than by the frontend container.

132:- Cookie domain rewrite: `proxy_cookie_domain nginx-gateway $host` — rewrites backend's `Domain=nginx-gateway` to the request host so the browser accepts it
133:- TLS terminates in nginx on port 443 for `wimsbfp.tech` using `/etc/letsencrypt/live/wimsbfp.tech/fullchain.pem` and `privkey.pem`
134:- Gateway security headers: nginx disables version tokens, hides proxied `X-Powered-By`, and adds HSTS, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, and a restrictive camera/microphone permissions policy while allowing same-origin geolocation.
137:- `/health` is served directly by nginx from the HTTPS server block for gateway uptime checks. The frontend also exposes a Next.js `/health` route for direct `npm run dev`/frontend-only runs; nginx takes precedence in Docker deployments.

"""Regression tests for reverse-proxy client IP header handling.

PR #446 P1-8: the prior version of this test only inspected
``nginx.conf``, so the 5-line ``set_real_ip_from 172.16.0.0/12`` widening
and the missing ``Access-Control-Expose-Headers: Retry-After`` directive
in ``nginx.ci.conf`` and ``nginx.local.conf`` passed CI. We now
parameterize over all three configs so drift in any of them fails the
build.

The carve-out below documents the intentional asymmetry:
- Public surfaces ``/api/v1/public/`` and ``/api/civilian/`` MUST use
  ``$realip_remote_addr`` (the pre-real-IP-module socket address) so the
  backend rate limiter cannot be bypassed by a spoofed X-Forwarded-For
  header (gap #14 / DS-07).
- Authenticated ``/api/``, ``/auth/``, and ``/`` blocks historically used
  ``$remote_addr`` for X-Real-IP. As of 2026-06-22, ALL location blocks
  (including ``/api/auth/``) use ``$realip_remote_addr`` for X-Real-IP as
  defense-in-depth against the internal/SSRF vector. ``/api/auth/callback``
  is pre-auth PKCE — the old "behind a JWT/session" rationale did not apply
  to it. X-Forwarded-For directives are unchanged (trusted_client_ip never
  reads XFF).
"""

# CI Pre-flight Routine

Run this routine in full before every push or PR on this repo.
All four CI gates are blocking (`merge-gate` fails if any one fails).

---

## Gate 1 — Backend ruff lint

```bash
cd src/backend
ruff check .
```

**If it fails:** ruff prints `file.py:line:col: Exxxx message`. Fix each one.
Common issues:

| Code | Meaning | Fix |
|------|---------|-----|
| `F401` | Unused import | Remove the import or add `# noqa: F401` only if re-exported intentionally |
| `F821` | Undefined name | Check spelling; add missing import |
| `E711` | `== None` instead of `is None` | Change to `is None` / `is not None` |
| `W291/W293` | Trailing whitespace | Delete trailing spaces |
| `E302/E303` | Wrong blank-line count | Two blank lines before top-level defs |

After fixing, re-run `ruff check .` until it exits 0.

---

## Gate 2 — Backend ruff format

```bash
cd src/backend
ruff format --check .
```

**If it fails:** run the formatter to auto-fix, then review the diff:

```bash
ruff format .
git diff
```

`ruff format` enforces: double quotes, 4-space indent, trailing commas in multi-line
collections, blank lines around class bodies. It does NOT sort imports — that is
handled by `ruff check` (rule `I`). The project does NOT enable `I` rules, so import
order is not enforced; do not add isort or reorder imports unnecessarily.

After formatting, re-run `ruff format --check .` until it exits 0.

---

## Gate 3 — Backend pytest

CI command (mirrors `ci.yml` exactly):

```bash
cd src/backend
pytest -v --tb=short \
  --ignore=tests/test_rate_limiting.py \
  --ignore=tests/test_suricata_ingestion.py \
  --ignore=tests/test_infra_config.py \
  --ignore=tests/integration/test_wims_initial_schema_bootstrap.py \
  --ignore=tests/integration/test_auth_otp_policy.py \
  --ignore=tests/integration/test_database_schema.py \
  --ignore=tests/integration/test_rls_policy_enforcement.py \
  --ignore=tests/integration/test_sql_quality_audit.py
```

The `addopts` in `pytest.ini` already include the same `--ignore` list, so
`pytest -v` locally is equivalent. Use the explicit form above to exactly match CI.

**Required environment variables** (CI injects these; set locally for integration tests):

```bash
export DATABASE_URL="postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/wims_test"
export REDIS_URL="redis://localhost:6379/0"
export KEYCLOAK_REALM_URL="http://localhost:8080/auth/realms/bfp"
export KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_ID="bfp-client"
export KEYCLOAK_AUDIENCE="account"
export WIMS_MASTER_KEY="<32-byte hex key>"
```

### Common test failure patterns

**UUID passed where string expected**
Symptom: `AttributeError: 'UUID' object has no attribute 'replace'`
Fix: In fixture dependency overrides, always `str()` UUID values:
```python
async def _async_override():
    return {"user_id": str(user_id), "keycloak_id": str(keycloak_id)}
```

**RLS context not set after commit**
Symptom: queries return 0 rows after a `db.commit()` mid-handler.
Cause: `SET LOCAL wims.current_user_id` resets when the transaction commits.
Fix: call `set_rls_context(db, user_id)` again after every `db.commit()` in the
same handler (see `incidents.py` and `regional.py` for the pattern).

**Fixture using wrong session factory**
Symptom: INSERT in fixture succeeds but the row is invisible to the handler.
Cause: test seeding used `_SessionLocal` (app URL, RLS-gated) instead of
`_AdminSessionLocal` (admin URL, bypasses RLS).
Fix: seed test data through `_AdminSessionLocal` from `database.py`.

**Import errors on collection**
Symptom: `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'auth'`
Cause: running pytest outside `src/backend/` — `pythonpath = .` in `pytest.ini`
resolves relative to that directory.
Fix: always run pytest from `src/backend/`.

---

## Gate 4 — Frontend

```bash
cd src/frontend
npm run lint          # ESLint — must exit 0 (warnings OK, errors block)
npx vitest run        # all tests must pass
npm run build         # production build must succeed
```

Build requires these env vars (CI sets them; safe dummy values work locally):

```bash
export NEXT_PUBLIC_AUTH_API_URL="http://localhost:8080/auth/realms/bfp"
export NEXT_PUBLIC_MAPBOX_TOKEN=""
export NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL="http://localhost"
```

---

## Gate 5 — SQL migrations (optional locally, always runs in CI)

CI applies every `.sql` file in `src/postgres-init/` in strict lexical order
with `ON_ERROR_STOP=1`. If you added or edited a migration file:

```bash
# spin up a throw-away postgres and replay all migrations
export PGPASSWORD=postgres
for f in $(ls src/postgres-init/*.sql | LC_ALL=C sort); do
  echo "Applying $f"
  psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -h localhost -p 5432 -U postgres -d wims_test -f "$f"
done
```

Common SQL failures: duplicate object names (add `IF NOT EXISTS` / `OR REPLACE`),
missing schema prefix (`wims.` before table names), `CREATE POLICY` on a table
that does not yet have `ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`.

---

## Recommended pre-push sequence

```bash
# 1. Fix lint
cd src/backend && ruff check . && ruff format --check .
# If format check fails:
#   ruff format . && git add -u && git diff --staged

# 2. Run tests
cd src/backend && pytest -v --tb=short

# 3. Frontend
cd src/frontend && npm run lint && npx vitest run && npm run build

# 4. Commit only if all three pass
git status
git add <specific files>
git commit -m "..."
git push
```

Never skip ruff format — it is the single most common CI blocker on this repo.
Run `ruff format .` (auto-fix) rather than hand-fixing whitespace.

stuck_ids=$(docker ps -a --filter 'status=created' --format '{{.ID}} {{.Names}}' | awk '$2 ~ /^wims-/ {print $1}')
              if [ -n "$stuck_ids" ]; then
                echo "Removing stale WIMS containers stuck in created state..."
                echo "$stuck_ids" | xargs -r docker rm -f
              fi

              # 3. Remove failed one-shot dependency containers. These services
              #    are safe to recreate and can otherwise keep compose --wait
              #    pinned to a previous failed DNS/startup attempt.
              oneshot_ids=$(docker ps -a --filter 'status=exited' --filter 'status=dead' --format '{{.ID}} {{.Names}}' | awk '$2 ~ /^wims-(ollama-model-pull|openbao-bootstrap)$/ {print $1}')
              if [ -n "$oneshot_ids" ]; then
                echo "Removing stale failed WIMS one-shot containers..."
                echo "$oneshot_ids" | xargs -r docker rm -f
              fi
            }

            echo "Validating production compose configuration..."
            compose config --quiet
            cleanup_stale_compose_renames

            # Pre-deploy DB connectivity check
            echo "Checking database connectivity..."
            compose exec -T postgres psql -U postgres -d wims -c "SELECT 1;" >/dev/null || { echo 'DB connectivity check failed — aborting deploy'; exit 1; }

            # Build and restart with retry. Stale Docker Compose renamed
            # containers (<hex>_wims-<service>) from a prior interrupted
            # deploy can block container creation with "container name is
            # already in use".  Clean up before and, if the first attempt
            # fails, clean up again and retry once.
            echo "Building and restarting production stack..."
            MAX_RETRIES=2
            BUILD_ATTEMPT=0
            while [ $BUILD_ATTEMPT -lt $MAX_RETRIES ]; do
              BUILD_ATTEMPT=$((BUILD_ATTEMPT + 1))
              cleanup_stale_compose_renames
              if compose up -d --build --wait --wait-timeout 600 2>/dev/null; then
                echo "Compose stack is up (attempt $BUILD_ATTEMPT)"
                break
              fi
              echo "Compose up failed (attempt $BUILD_ATTEMPT/$MAX_RETRIES) — cleaning stale containers and retrying..."
              if [ $BUILD_ATTEMPT -ge $MAX_RETRIES ]; then
                echo "Compose up failed after $MAX_RETRIES attempts — aborting deploy"
                exit 1
              fi
              cleanup_stale_compose_renames
              sleep 5
            done

            # ─── Wait for postgres to be ready ────────────────────────────────
            echo "Waiting for postgres..."
            for i in $(seq 1 30); do
              if compose exec -T postgres pg_isready -U postgres >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "Postgres ready"
                break
              fi
              sleep 1
            done

            # ─── Apply new database migrations (idempotent — all use IF NOT EXISTS) ───
            echo "Applying database migrations..."
            for script in $(ls -v /opt/wims-bfp/src/postgres-init/*.sql 2>/dev/null); do
              script_name=$(basename "$script")
              echo "  Running: $script_name"
              compose exec -T postgres psql -U postgres -d wims -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f "/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/$script_name" || {
                echo "Migration failed: $script_name — continuing"
              }
            done

            # ─── Reload nginx to refresh container DNS caches ───────────────
            # Run this BEFORE the post-deploy health check.  When containers are
            # recreated, Docker assigns new IPs and nginx's upstream zone caches
            # the old IP until the resolver TTL expires (10 s with ":10s" in the
            # resolver directive).  A reload forces immediate re-resolution so
            # the health check talks to the right containers.
            echo "Reloading nginx to flush DNS cache..."
            docker exec wims-nginx-gateway nginx -s reload || echo "Warning: nginx reload failed"
            sleep 3

            # ─── Post-deploy health check ───────────────────────────────────────
            echo "Waiting for backend to be ready..."
            sleep 15
            BACKEND_READY=0
            for i in $(seq 1 45); do
              if docker exec wims-backend python -c "import httpx; httpx.get('http://localhost:8000/health', timeout=5).raise_for_status()" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "Backend /health check passed"
                BACKEND_READY=1
                break
              fi
              echo "Attempt $i/45: backend not ready yet..."
              sleep 2
            done

            if [ "$BACKEND_READY" = "0" ]; then
              echo "Backend health check failed — initiating rollback"
              docker tag src-backend-rollback:latest src-backend:latest 2>/dev/null || true
              compose up -d backend
              echo "Rollback complete"
              exit 1
            fi

            echo "Checking public gateway health..."
            curl -fsS https://wimsbfp.tech/health >/dev/null
            curl -fsS https://wimsbfp.tech/auth/realms/bfp/.well-known/openid-configuration >/dev/null
            # Frontend route check — catches stale nginx DNS cache for frontend
            # upstream that the Keycloak and API probes cannot detect.
            curl -fsS https://wimsbfp.tech/login >/dev/null
            # This route traverses nginx -> backend and catches stale Docker DNS
            # upstreams that the nginx-served /health endpoint cannot detect.
            curl -fsS https://wimsbfp.tech/api/public/emergency-services >/dev/null

            echo "Checking Ollama model provisioning..."
            docker exec wims-ollama ollama list | grep -q 'qwen2.5:3b'

            echo "Deploy successful — commit $DEPLOY_COMMIT"
            echo "DEPLOY_COMMIT=$DEPLOY_COMMIT $(date -u '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')" >> /opt/wims-bfp/.deploy_history

## [2026-06-30] fix(ci): isolate Compose dynamic IPs from static host mappings

- **Scope:** PR #487 CI follow-up. GitHub Actions Security Scan failed during `docker compose up -d --build` with Docker daemon `Address already in use` immediately after one-shot/dynamic services started and before the full stack reached nginx. The failure is consistent with dynamic Compose network allocations colliding with low static IPs that are only claimed when their containers start.
- **Files modified:**
  - `src/docker-compose.yml` — keep `wims_internal` on `172.18.0.0/24`, add `ipam.config.ip_range: 172.18.0.128/25` for dynamic containers, remove the unnecessary static IP from `celery-worker`, and remove the temporary `backend -> celery-worker` startup dependency.
  - `src/backend/tests/test_suricata_redis_host_networking.py` — update the subnet contract to `/24` and add a regression test proving the dynamic `ip_range` does not overlap static service IPs.
  - `src/nginx/nginx.conf`, `src/nginx/nginx.local.conf`, `src/nginx/nginx.ci.conf` — narrow `set_real_ip_from` from `172.18.0.0/16` to the configured `172.18.0.0/24` bridge subnet.
  - `src/backend/tests/test_nginx_forwarded_headers.py` — pin the `/24` real-IP trust range so it stays aligned with Compose.
  - `system-wiki/architecture/infrastructure-config.md`, `system-wiki/security/asvs-l2-state.json` — document the static-low/dynamic-high IPAM layout and nginx trusted proxy range.
- **Behavior:** Static host mappings remain stable for redis/postgres/ollama/keycloak/openbao, while dynamic services (mailhog, bootstraps, model-pull, backend, celery, frontend, nginx) are allocated from `172.18.0.128/25`, avoiding Docker 28/Compose parallel-start address collisions in CI. Nginx's trusted proxy range now matches the `/24` bridge instead of trusting the broader `/16`.

## [2026-06-30] fix(ci): isolate Compose dynamic IPs from static host mappings

- **Scope:** PR #487 CI follow-up. GitHub Actions Security Scan failed during `docker compose up -d --build` with Docker daemon `Address already in use` immediately after one-shot/dynamic services started and before the full stack reached nginx. The failure is consistent with dynamic Compose network allocations colliding with low static IPs that are only claimed when their containers start.
- **Files modified:**
  - `src/docker-compose.yml` — keep `wims_internal` on `172.18.0.0/24`, add `ipam.config.ip_range: 172.18.0.128/25` for dynamic containers, remove the unnecessary static IP from `celery-worker`, and remove the temporary `backend -> celery-worker` startup dependency.
  - `src/backend/tests/test_suricata_redis_host_networking.py` — update the subnet contract to `/24` and add a regression test proving the dynamic `ip_range` does not overlap static service IPs.
  - `src/nginx/nginx.conf`, `src/nginx/nginx.local.conf`, `src/nginx/nginx.ci.conf` — narrow `set_real_ip_from` from `172.18.0.0/16` to the configured `172.18.0.0/24` bridge subnet.
  - `src/backend/tests/test_nginx_forwarded_headers.py` — pin the `/24` real-IP trust range so it stays aligned with Compose.
  - `system-wiki/architecture/infrastructure-config.md`, `system-wiki/security/asvs-l2-state.json` — document the static-low/dynamic-high IPAM layout and nginx trusted proxy range.
- **Behavior:** Static host mappings remain stable for redis/postgres/ollama/keycloak/openbao, while dynamic services (mailhog, bootstraps, model-pull, backend, celery, frontend, nginx) are allocated from `172.18.0.128/25`, avoiding Docker 28/Compose parallel-start address collisions in CI. Nginx's trusted proxy range now matches the `/24` bridge instead of trusting the broader `/16`.
- **Validation:**
  - `cd src/backend && pytest tests/test_suricata_redis_host_networking.py tests/test_nginx_forwarded_headers.py -q` — 26 passed.
  - `cd src/backend && ruff check tests/test_suricata_redis_host_networking.py tests/test_nginx_forwarded_headers.py && ruff format --check tests/test_suricata_redis_host_networking.py tests/test_nginx_forwarded_headers.py` — clean.

  - `/tmp/repro/iprange-race.yml` local Compose reproduction with the same static-low/dynamic-high pattern — 12 alpine containers started concurrently without `Address already in use`, then were torn down.

summary:
## Goal
Fix PR#487 CI failure where `docker compose up` fails with Docker daemon "Address already in use" during parallel startup. The root cause is dynamic Compose IP allocations colliding with low static IPs (assigned to redis, postgres, etc.) when containers start concurrently.

## Constraints & Preferences
- Must preserve static IPs needed by `extra_hosts` entries (redis, postgres, keycloak, ollama, openbao) for Suricata/botstrap connectivity
- CI preflight not run locally before push (deferred to GitHub Actions)
- Minimal diff, no unrelated refactors

## Progress
### Done
- [x] Diagnosed root cause: Compose dynamic allocator can assign addresses from the low end of the subnet, colliding with static IPs that are only claimed when their container starts
- [x] Added `ipam.config.ip_range: 172.18.0.128/25` to `wims_internal` network in `src/docker-compose.yml`
- [x] Removed unnecessary static IP `172.18.0.10` from `celery-worker`
- [x] Removed temporary `backend→celery-worker` depends_on condition
- [x] Narrowed `set_real_ip_from` in all 3 nginx configs (`nginx.conf`, `nginx.ci.conf`, `nginx.local.conf`) from `172.18.0.0/16` to `172.18.0.0/24`
- [x] Updated contract tests: added `test_wims_internal_dynamic_ip_range_avoids_static_ips`, pinned subnet to `/24`, pinned nginx trust range to `/24`
- [x] Updated system-wiki: `infrastructure-config.md`, `log.md`, `asvs-l2-state.json`
- [x] Committed as `800a159 fix(ci): isolate compose dynamic IP range` and pushed
- [x] GitHub Actions run `28423580879` passed (all jobs including Security Scan)
- [x] Cleaned up local reproduction files (`/tmp/repro/`, `/tmp/aux-test/`, `/tmp/iprange-test/`) and leftover Docker resources

### In Progress
- (none)

### Blocked
- PR `mergeStateStatus` is `BLOCKED` (not CI-related – likely branch protection or admin condition)

## Key Decisions
- **Dynamic IP isolation via `ip_range`**: Keep static IPs low (172.18.0.3–0.8), keep dynamic allocator in 172.18.0.128/25 to eliminate race during parallel Compose startup. Avoids need for service serialization or full CI override.
- **Remove celery-worker static IP**: Unnecessary – celery-worker has `networks: wims_internal` (bridged) so Docker DNS resolves hostnames without extra_hosts.
- **Remove backend→celery-worker depends_on**: Backend doesn't need celery to start; this was a temporary workaround that didn't fix the root cause.
- **Narrow nginx `set_real_ip_from` to /24**: Aligns with the narrower Compose subnet; reduces attack surface by trusting 65,280 fewer addresses than the previous /16.

## Next Steps
1. Unblock PR merge (requires admin action on branch protection settings or rebase onto master if behind)
2. Consider running full CI pre-flight locally if further changes are needed (skipped this session per user request to push immediately)

## Critical Context
- The reproduction at `/tmp/repro/no-iprange-race.yml` (low static IPs without dynamic range split) consistently reproduced Docker "Address already in use". With `ip_range: 172.18.0.128/25`, 12 alpine containers started cleanly in parallel.

name: Deploy to VPS on master

on:
  push:
    branches: [master]

jobs:
  # ─── CI Gate ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  ci:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      NEXT_PUBLIC_AUTH_API_URL: ${{ vars.NEXT_PUBLIC_AUTH_API_URL }}
      NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL: ${{ vars.NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL }}
      KEYCLOAK_REALM_URL: "http://localhost:8080/auth/realms/bfp"
      KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_ID: "wims-web"
      KEYCLOAK_AUDIENCE: "wims-web"
      DATABASE_URL: "postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/wims_test"
      REDIS_URL: "redis://localhost:6379/0"
      WIMS_MASTER_KEY: ${{ secrets.WIMS_MASTER_KEY }}
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgis/postgis:15-3.4-alpine
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: postgres
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres
          POSTGRES_DB: wims_test
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd pg_isready
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5

      redis:
        image: redis:7-alpine
        ports:
          - 6379:6379
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "redis-cli ping"
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'
          cache: 'npm'
          cache-dependency-path: src/frontend/package-lock.json

      - name: Install frontend deps
        run: npm ci
        working-directory: src/frontend

      - name: Run frontend build
        run: npm run build
        working-directory: src/frontend

      - name: Run frontend lint
        run: npm run lint
        working-directory: src/frontend

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.10'
          cache: 'pip'
          cache-dependency-path: src/backend/requirements.txt

      - name: Install backend deps
        run: pip install -r src/backend/requirements.txt

      - name: Wait for PostgreSQL
        run: |
          for i in $(seq 1 30); do
            pg_isready -h localhost -U postgres && echo "PostgreSQL ready" && break
            echo "Waiting... ($i/30)"
            sleep 1
          done

      - name: Initialize test database
        run: |
          export PGPASSWORD=postgres
          find "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/src/postgres-init" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.sql' -print0 \
            | LC_ALL=C sort -z \
            | while IFS= read -r -d '' script; do
                echo "Applying: ${script#$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/}"
                psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -h localhost -p 5432 -U postgres -d wims_test \
                  -f "$script"
              done

      - name: Run backend tests
        run: pytest -v --tb=short --ignore=tests/test_rate_limiting.py --ignore=tests/test_suricata_ingestion.py --ignore=tests/integration/test_wims_initial_schema_bootstrap.py --ignore=tests/integration/test_auth_otp_policy.py --ignore=tests/integration/test_database_schema.py --ignore=tests/integration/test_rls_policy_enforcement.py --ignore=tests/integration/test_sql_quality_audit.py
        working-directory: src/backend

  # ─── Deploy (only if CI passes) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
  deploy:

deploy:
    needs: [ci]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      DATABASE_URL: ${{ secrets.DATABASE_URL }}
      REDIS_URL: ${{ secrets.REDIS_URL }}
      KEYCLOAK_REALM_URL: ${{ secrets.KEYCLOAK_REALM_URL }}
      KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_ID: "wims-web"
      KEYCLOAK_AUDIENCE: "wims-web"
      WIMS_MASTER_KEY: ${{ secrets.WIMS_MASTER_KEY }}
      FIREBASE_CREDENTIALS_PATH: ${{ secrets.FIREBASE_CREDENTIALS_PATH }}
      KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD }}
      KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_CLIENT_SECRET: ${{ secrets.KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_CLIENT_SECRET }}
      DEPLOY_COMMIT: ${{ github.sha }}
    steps:
      - name: Provision TLS certificate via certbot
        uses: appleboy/ssh-action@v1.0.3
        with:
          host: ${{ secrets.VPS_HOST }}
          username: wims
          key: ${{ secrets.VPS_SSH_KEY }}
          script: |
            set -euo pipefail

            if ! command -v certbot &> /dev/null; then
              echo "Installing certbot..."
              sudo apt-get update -qq
              sudo apt-get install -y -qq certbot
            fi

            if [ ! -s /etc/letsencrypt/live/wimsbfp.tech/fullchain.pem ] || [ ! -s /etc/letsencrypt/live/wimsbfp.tech/privkey.pem ]; then
              echo "No wimsbfp.tech certificate found; issuing initial certificate with standalone ACME challenge..."
              docker stop wims-nginx-gateway >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
              sudo certbot certonly \
                --standalone \
                --non-interactive \
                --agree-tos \
                --email x1n4te@proton.me \
                --domains wimsbfp.tech \
                --cert-name wimsbfp.tech \
                --keep-until-expiring
            else
              echo "Existing wimsbfp.tech certificate found; skipping issuance."
            fi

            printf 'SHELL=/bin/sh\nPATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/sbin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin\n0 0,12 * * * root certbot renew --quiet --deploy-hook "docker exec wims-nginx-gateway nginx -s reload"\n' | sudo tee /etc/cron.d/certbot-renewal >/dev/null
            echo "Certbot auto-renewal cron installed."

      - name: Tag previous image for rollback
        uses: appleboy/ssh-action@v1.0.3
        with:
          host: ${{ secrets.VPS_HOST }}
          username: wims
          key: ${{ secrets.VPS_SSH_KEY }}
          script: |
            cd /opt/wims-bfp/src
            compose() {
              docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml --env-file .env.production "$@"
            }

            PREV_IMAGE=$(compose images -q backend | head -n 1)
            if [ -n "$PREV_IMAGE" ]; then
              echo "Tagging previous backend image for rollback: $PREV_IMAGE"
              docker tag "$PREV_IMAGE" src-backend-rollback:latest
            else
              echo "No existing backend image found — skipping rollback tag"
            fi

      - name: Deploy via SSH
        uses: appleboy/ssh-action@v1.0.3
        with:
          host: ${{ secrets.VPS_HOST }}
          username: wims
          key: ${{ secrets.VPS_SSH_KEY }}
          envs: DATABASE_URL,REDIS_URL,KEYCLOAK_REALM_URL,KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_ID,KEYCLOAK_AUDIENCE,WIMS_MASTER_KEY,FIREBASE_CREDENTIALS_PATH,KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD,KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_CLIENT_SECRET,DEPLOY_COMMIT
          timeout: 15m
          command_timeout: 20m
          script: |
            set -euo pipefail

            export DATABASE_URL="$DATABASE_URL"
            export REDIS_URL="$REDIS_URL"
            export KEYCLOAK_REALM_URL="$KEYCLOAK_REALM_URL"
            export KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_ID="$KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_ID"
            export KEYCLOAK_AUDIENCE="$KEYCLOAK_AUDIENCE"
            export WIMS_MASTER_KEY="$WIMS_MASTER_KEY"
            export FIREBASE_CREDENTIALS_PATH="$FIREBASE_CREDENTIALS_PATH"
            export KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD="$KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD"
            export KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_CLIENT_SECRET="$KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_CLIENT_SECRET"
            export DEPLOY_COMMIT="$DEPLOY_COMMIT"

            cd /opt/wims-bfp
            git fetch origin master
            git reset --hard
            git clean -fd
            git checkout -B master origin/master
            cd src

            test -f .env.production || { echo ".env.production is missing on VPS"; exit 1; }

            compose() {
              docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml --env-file .env.production "$@"
            }

            cleanup_stale_compose_renames() {
              # Docker Compose renames old fixed-container-name services to
              # <hash>_wims-<service> during recreate. If a prior deploy is
              # interrupted, a stale renamed container can block future recreates
              # with "container name ... is already in use".
              # The project name is derived from the working directory (src/).

              # 1. Remove stale renamed containers (<hash>_wims-<service>)
              stale_ids=$(docker ps -aq --filter 'label=com.docker.compose.project=src' --format '{{.ID}} {{.Names}}' | awk '$2 ~ /^[0-9a-f]+_wims-/ {print $1}')
              if [ -n "$stale_ids" ]; then
                echo "Removing stale Compose-renamed WIMS containers..."
                echo "$stale_ids" | xargs -r docker rm -f
              fi

              # 2. Remove fixed-name WIMS containers stuck in "created" state
              #    (never started — always from an interrupted deploy)
              stuck_ids=$(docker ps -a --filter 'status=created' --format '{{.ID}} {{.Names}}' | awk '$2 ~ /^wims-/ {print $1}')
              if [ -n "$stuck_ids" ]; then
                echo "Removing stale WIMS containers stuck in created state..."
                echo "$stuck_ids" | xargs -r docker rm -f
              fi

              # 3. Remove failed one-shot dependency containers. These services
              #    are safe to recreate and can otherwise keep compose --wait
              #    pinned to a previous failed DNS/startup attempt.
              oneshot_ids=$(docker ps -a --filter 'status=exited' --filter 'status=dead' --format '{{.ID}} {{.Names}}' | awk '$2 ~ /^wims-(ollama-model-pull|openbao-bootstrap)$/ {print $1}')
              if [ -n "$oneshot_ids" ]; then
                echo "Removing stale failed WIMS one-shot containers..."
                echo "$oneshot_ids" | xargs -r docker rm -f
              fi
            }

            echo "Validating production compose configuration..."
            compose config --quiet
            cleanup_stale_compose_renames

            # Pre-deploy DB connectivity check
            echo "Checking database connectivity..."
            compose exec -T postgres psql -U postgres -d wims -c "SELECT 1;" >/dev/null || { echo 'DB connectivity check failed — aborting deploy'; exit 1; }

            # Build and restart with retry. Stale Docker Compose renamed
            # containers (<hex>_wims-<service>) from a prior interrupted
            # deploy can block container creation with "container name is
            # already in use".  Clean up before and, if the first attempt
            # fails, clean up again and retry once.
            echo "Building and restarting production stack..."
            MAX_RETRIES=2

MAX_RETRIES=2
            BUILD_ATTEMPT=0
            while [ $BUILD_ATTEMPT -lt $MAX_RETRIES ]; do
              BUILD_ATTEMPT=$((BUILD_ATTEMPT + 1))
              cleanup_stale_compose_renames
              if compose up -d --build --wait --wait-timeout 600 2>/dev/null; then
                echo "Compose stack is up (attempt $BUILD_ATTEMPT)"
                break
              fi
              echo "Compose up failed (attempt $BUILD_ATTEMPT/$MAX_RETRIES) — cleaning stale containers and retrying..."
              if [ $BUILD_ATTEMPT -ge $MAX_RETRIES ]; then
                echo "Compose up failed after $MAX_RETRIES attempts — aborting deploy"
                exit 1
              fi
              cleanup_stale_compose_renames
              sleep 5
            done

            # ─── Wait for postgres to be ready ────────────────────────────────
            echo "Waiting for postgres..."
            for i in $(seq 1 30); do
              if compose exec -T postgres pg_isready -U postgres >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "Postgres ready"
                break
              fi
              sleep 1
            done

            # ─── Apply new database migrations (idempotent — all use IF NOT EXISTS) ───
            echo "Applying database migrations..."
            for script in $(ls -v /opt/wims-bfp/src/postgres-init/*.sql 2>/dev/null); do
              script_name=$(basename "$script")
              echo "  Running: $script_name"
              compose exec -T postgres psql -U postgres -d wims -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f "/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/$script_name" || {
                echo "Migration failed: $script_name — continuing"

            sleep 15
            BACKEND_READY=0
            for i in $(seq 1 45); do
